summary: All claimed acceptance evidence is genuine and I reproduced it independently: gate 6/6 PASS exit 0; --expect-red exit 1; archived baseline 0/6 exit 1; tsc --noEmit exit 0; queueStore.ts sha256 = 0a88a6735c27b2fc2452fc02cc62af0234b8a0e7be4e1882c9bd8ea0e484feb6 (= candidate digest input), and every file in the candidate snapshot hashes as recorded. The guard in queueStore.enqueue genuinely satisfies the six explicit manual constraints: it never consults `paused` (constraint a), it is synchronous inside enqueue with no await (b), it admits a click's whole batch via an index-continuation chain (c), it matches only queued||running and never historical jobs (d)(e), and it is keyed per nodeId, not global (f) — I verified each with my own out-of-repo probes and by reading the code. Nevertheless a further false-green class remains, and REQ-001 is only half-fixed, so this candidate must not be accepted. (1) REQ-001's user-visible half is still broken: recovery clears data.queued on the flowStore copy only — flowStore is not persisted, so it is empty at recovery time and that write is a no-op — while the copy that actually survives the restart lives in canvasStore, where updateNodeQueuedState returns early for the active canvas (queueStore.ts:433). The stale queued=true is therefore re-loaded into flowStore by App's canvas-load effect and the node still shows 排队中 with the generate button disabled after restart. The gate cannot see this because its case A pre-populates flowStore before importing queueStore (scripts/queue-regression.mjs:388-398) and asserts only that copy (:414-415); its job-status assertion still passes because the dispatched job falls to error(节点不存在). (2) The new rejection contract (enqueue returns "") is ignored by its only production caller: useImageGeneratorExecution.ts:86-90 unconditionally writes {queued:true,status:"idle"} after the enqueue loop, so a guard-rejected click still marks the node queued; because the executor only clears that flag when a job starts (imageGenerationExecution.ts:265-272) and not on success (:414-423), a rejection landing after the node's last job started locks the node permanently — reproduced deterministically 3/3. (3) The guard keys on nodeId alone while duplicate-canvas preserves node ids, so a legitimate generation on another canvas is silently rejected. Findings 1-3 are behavioural and were established with out-of-repo probes that drive the real stores/hook (node --experimental-strip-types, repo React/tsconfig aliases, faithful executor stubs); no repository file was modified, no GUI was run, hence ui_review is null.
findings: REQ-001 NOT FIXED (user-visible half) — location: src/stores/queueStore.ts:190-209 (recoverPersistedQueuedJobs) + :421-449 (updateNodeQueuedState, early return at :433) + :405-415 (onRehydrateStorage). Trigger: any real cold start where the leftover queued job's canvasId equals the persisted activeCanvasId — i.e. exactly the REQ-001 scenario. (a) flowStore is not a persisted store (no persist/createJSONStorage in src/stores/flowStore.ts), so at recovery time flowStore.nodes is empty and the flowStore branch of updateNodeQueuedState has nothing to write; (b) the canvasStore branch is the only one that could clear the persisted copy, and it returns early at :433 when canvasId === activeCanvasId, which is the normal case because the job stores activeCanvasId (useImageGeneratorExecution.ts:65) and canvasStore persists activeCanvasId (src/stores/canvasStore.ts:215-218); (c) waitForCanvasReady returns as soon as canvasStore._hasHydrated is true (:176), so the dispatch is not held back for flowStore to load, and readNodeFromCanvas (imageGenerationExecution.ts:92-99) then reads flowStore for the active canvas, finds no node, and returns 节点不存在 without writing queued — so the job does reach a non-queued terminal state (which is why the gate's job assertion passes) while the node flag is untouched; (d) App's canvas-load effect (src/App.tsx:121-163, setNodes(canvas.nodes)) runs after React's commit and therefore after recovery's microtask-fast continuation, loading the stale queued=true back into flowStore, which is what ImageGeneratorNode.tsx:174/215 reads to compute canRun. Impact: after restart the node permanently displays 排队中 with the generate button disabled (ImageGeneratorNode.tsx:250 disabled={!canRun}; ImageGeneratorInspector.tsx:646-651 the same), and no queued job remains for recovery to process on the next restart — REQ-001's stated symptom survives unchanged. Evidence: out-of-repo probes reproduced the locked branch at App-load delays 0/50/100/200/900/1200ms (executor dispatch always preceded app-setNodes; final flowStore.data.queued=true, canvasStore.data.queued=true, canRun=false), stable 3/3 on repeat. This is a race, and I checked the losing branch honestly: if queueStore's hydration loses to canvasStore's by more than a full React render, the flag is cleared on flowStore first and App's 800ms debounced write-back then cleans the canvas too, so the node recovers (my reverse-order probe confirms this self-heals). The default evaluation order is the failing one: (1) canvasStore is evaluated before queueStore (App.tsx:5 imports Toolbar, Toolbar.tsx:4 imports flowStore, flowStore.ts:20 imports canvasStore, Toolbar.tsx:6 imports queueStore), so canvasStore's persist read is issued first; (2) both reads resolve together off the same shared store-init promise (tauriStorage.ts:14-46); (3) recovery needs only microtasks for its dynamic imports, whereas App's setNodes needs a React render commit plus an effect after canvasStore hydration. So queueStore's recovery wins the race in practice, for every job whose canvasId is null or equal to the persisted activeCanvasId — which is the normal case, since the hook stamps the active canvasId at enqueue time (useImageGeneratorExecution.ts:65). I checked the losing branch honestly: when the job's canvasId belongs to a non-active canvas, the executor resolves the node from canvasStore (readNodeFromCanvas) and its start-up write clears the flag on that canvas copy (updateNodeDataWithCanvas at imageGenerationExecution.ts:265-272), so that variant does not lock; and when flowStore happens to be loaded first (e.g. a canvas switch restoring nodes before recovery fires), the flag is cleared on flowStore and App's 800ms debounced write-back cleans the canvas too, which my reverse-order probe confirms self-heals. The defect is therefore scheduling-dependent but its default branch is the failing one, and it covers both the gate's own seed shape (canvasId null: the canvas copy is never touched, because updateNodeQueuedState skips the canvas branch entirely when canvasId is falsy) and the active-canvas shape. Suggestion: clear the flag on the persisted copy too — e.g. drop the canvasId === activeCanvasId early return for a queued:false write (or write directly into canvases for the active canvas as well), and/or make waitForCanvasReady wait for the node to be resolvable in flowStore for active-canvas jobs instead of returning on _hasHydrated alone; then extend the gate's case A to (i) not pre-populate flowStore, (ii) seed canvasStore, and (iii) assert the node flag after modelling App's setNodes, plus assert the persisted copy is cleared.

NEW DEFECT INTRODUCED BY THE GUARD (can create the REQ-001 lock) — location: src/hooks/useImageGeneratorExecution.ts:61-90 (unconditional updateNodeData after the enqueue loop; return value ignored at :63 and :76) against src/stores/queueStore.ts:234 (guard returns "" for a rejected enqueue). Trigger: a click on a node that still has an active job, made while the button is enabled. Because the batch jobs of one node each write status on start/end while only the start path clears queued, the button becomes enabled between the first finished job (status success, queued not rewritten — imageGenerationExecution.ts:414-423) and the last still-active job; a second click in that window is rejected by the guard (job count does not grow: 2 to 2), but the hook still writes {queued:true,status:"idle"}. Impact: once the node's remaining jobs finish, no active job is left to clear the flag, so the node is permanently stuck on 排队中 with the button disabled; the queue panel offers nothing to cancel (no active job) and restart does not help (the flag is in the persisted canvas copy and the queue has no queued job for recovery to act on). This is the exact REQ-001 symptom, now reachable from ordinary repeated clicking, which is what REQ-002 was about. Evidence: out-of-repo probe drove the real hook with a faithful executor stub (n=2, concurrency=2): it captured the enabled-button window (active=1, queued=false, canRun=true), clicked, observed the guard reject (2 to 2 jobs) yet queued become true, then after all jobs ended observed active=0, queued=true, canRun=false — reproduced 3/3. The gate cannot see it: all six cases assert job counts (and case A's flag only in the cold-start scenario), never the node flag after a rejected click. Suggestion: make the hook honour the new contract — treat "" as not-enqueued and only write queued:true when at least one job was admitted (and clear it when all were rejected); alternatively have enqueue itself clear the node's queued marker when it rejects, so the contract no longer depends on every caller.

GUARD IS CANVAS-BLIND (nodeId only) — location: src/stores/queueStore.ts:101-108 (hasActiveJobForNode matches job.nodeId only) and :237 (batchChains keyed by job.nodeId), versus src/stores/canvasStore.ts:105-125 where duplicateCanvas copies { ...canvas } and keeps every node.id, exposed in UI at src/components/Sidebar.tsx:144-147. Trigger: duplicate a canvas (the copy's nodes keep the same ids), generate on canvas X, switch to canvas Y and click generate on the same-id node. Impact: the guard sees X's active job as belonging to the same node and rejects Y's legitimate click (silently — enqueue returns "", which the hook ignores), and by Finding 2 that rejection also stamps queued:true on Y's node, locking it. Jobs elsewhere in this module are canvas-aware (QueueJob.canvasId, readNodeFromCanvas, updateNodeDataWithCanvas), so this guard is the one canvas-blind component. Evidence: out-of-repo probe with the real hook: X click to 1 job (n=1) or 2 jobs (n=2), switch activeCanvasId to Y, click to 0 jobs on Y. Pre-existing duplication behaviour, not covered by any gate case (all cases use a single canvas or null canvasId). Suggestion: key both the active-job check and the batch chain by canvasId + nodeId (e.g. `${job.canvasId ?? ""}\u0001${job.nodeId}`), keeping null-canvas behaviour unchanged; add a gate case that duplicates a canvas and asserts each canvas admits its own batch.

LOW / latent fragility — module-level batch state carries an unenforced invariant. Location: src/stores/queueStore.ts:79-99 and :226-244. The continuation rule is correct only if a click's batch loop (useImageGeneratorExecution.ts:62-74) always runs to completion synchronously and always starts at batchIndex 1; nothing enforces either. In an out-of-repo probe, a batch that delivered only its first of 4 jobs (loop interrupted) followed by a new identical-shape click was misread: the new click's calls 2..4 matched the stale chain (nextIndex had advanced to 2) and 3 jobs were admitted in addition to the one already queued (expected 0 growth). Reachability today is low — the loop is synchronous and cannot throw (executeImageGeneration is async so it cannot throw synchronously; zustand subscribers do not throw) — so I am reporting this as latent rather than live. The same module state is also never pruned: batchChains gains one entry per distinct nodeId that ever starts a batch and is only deleted for the same nodeId on a later single/retry enqueue, and it is not reset on rehydration, while jobs themselves are capped at 200 (queueStore.ts:249). Suggestion: make the invariant explicit and self-checking rather than commented — e.g. store the remaining count for the batch alongside the shape key and drop the chain once the last index has been seen, or (better) pass the click's batch identity (a token/count) from the hook so continuation never depends on index arithmetic; clear batchChains in onRehydrateStorage, and document the invariant next to the loop in useImageGeneratorExecution.ts.

LOW / stale verification harness — scripts/queue-regression.selfcheck.mjs now reports 21/27. I ran it against this candidate: the six failures are 'default mode on unrepaired source must FAIL', '--expect-red must exit 0', 'entry-guard-running-only must FAIL', 'entry-guard-active must FAIL', 'partial-fix-job-only must FAIL', and the entry-guard precise-profile check. These are consequences of the fix living in the same working tree (the store-layer guard already de-duplicates, so layering an entry-level guard on top is no longer distinguishable; and the real recovery clears the flag, so partial-fix-job-only no longer demonstrates anything), not evidence that the gate itself regressed. Impact: the 'the assertions have teeth' evidence is not reproducible against this candidate — it requires the pre-fix revision — and the self-check's own baseline assertions cannot be run as a gate in the fixed state without failing. Suggestion: pin the mutant matrix to an explicit baseline revision (or a fixture copy of the pre-fix queueStore/hook) instead of the working tree, so teeth-evidence and the shipped candidate can be validated independently and repeatably.

review_checks.analysis: REQ-002 is substantively addressed for the behaviours the gate and my probes cover: the guard is synchronous inside queueStore.enqueue (no await between reading jobs at :223 and deciding at :226-244), covers the batch branch as a whole batch per click, covers retry (retry sets enqueueOriginRetry and calls enqueue at :277-288, reset in finally), covers non-awaited overlapping clicks and paused=true, matches only queued||running (never historical), is keyed by nodeId (not global) and does not lock regeneration after a batch completes. I verified each of these independently (probes: single-node triple-click 3 to 1; batch n=4 intact; second click admitted 0; paused=true still 1 and batch still 4; two nodes independent; history terminal then regenerate 4 new; retry 3x adds 1). REQ-001 is NOT fully fixed. The diff's own claim is that recovery clears the node's residual queued marker, but it only clears the flowStore copy: flowStore is not a persisted store, so at recovery time it holds no nodes and that write is a no-op; the copy that survives a restart is the one in the persisted canvasStore, and updateNodeQueuedState returns early for the active canvas (queueStore.ts:433), so it is never cleared — which is the normal case, because jobs record the active canvasId and canvasStore persists activeCanvasId. Recovery then dispatches against flowStore (readNodeFromCanvas prefers flowStore for the active canvas), gets 节点不存在, and the job lands in error — so the job half of REQ-001 is satisfied while the node half is not. On the onRehydrateStorage rewrite specifically: the previously unreachable branch (recovering status==='running', which partialize never writes — :401-404) is genuinely gone, and the new path is reachable (the callback now keys off the error argument and calls recoverPersistedQueuedJobs, which I observed firing on real hydration), so that part of the rewrite is sound; and the error-argument form is an improvement over the old `if (!state) return`. The diff is otherwise in scope: it adds recovery, the guard, batch-chain bookkeeping, and defensive .catch on the two best-effort dynamic imports (which prevents an unhandled rejection crash-loop during unattended recovery) — no unrelated behaviour changes beyond the package.json script aliases, which are additive. Scope-adjacent concern: because recovery now dispatches leftover queued jobs instead of only failing them, recovery can re-run a generation automatically on startup; that is the intended fix, but combined with Finding 1 the dispatched job fails with 节点不存在 rather than executing, so the user gains an error entry but keeps the locked node.

I reproduced every acceptance claim rather than trusting it. `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/queue-regression.mjs` gives PASS 6 / FAIL 0 / ERROR 0, exit 0, byte-identical in substance to the archived RUN-365a88f543cc472e8bf6faa479d069a6-behavior-regression.stdout.txt; `--expect-red` exits 1 (all six now green, so the red self-check correctly reports the defects are gone); the archived BASELINE-gate-red-TASK-006.txt shows 0/6 PASS exit 1 with the pre-fix symptom for each case, so the red-to-green claim is genuinely evidenced rather than asserted; `node ./node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit` exits 0 with empty stdout; and queueStore.ts hashes to 0a88a6735c27b2fc2452fc02cc62af0234b8a0e7be4e1882c9bd8ea0e484feb6, matching the candidate record, whose ten listed files all still hash as recorded. The assertions are largely load-bearing: case B/C/E/F assert time-independent job counts rather than instantaneous samples (fixing false-green class 1), case C covers the batch branch explicitly with a premise check and an ERROR-not-FAIL policy for slow execution, case D forces the queued-but-not-running state by occupying the concurrency slot with another node (fixing class 3), case E removes the await (fixing class 4's overlapping-click hole), and case F drives retry. I also confirmed by reading the script that it never consults process.env (the only matches are comments), so the historical NC_QUEUE_MUTANT forgery path is closed (class 2). What it still cannot see is the surviving class: case A is unfaithful to the app's data flow. It pre-populates flowStore before importing queueStore (:388-398) and asserts the flag only on useFlowStore (:414-415, :449); it never seeds or inspects canvasStore (grep for useCanvasStore / next-creator-canvases in the gate returns nothing) and never models App's canvas-load effect. Its ① job-disposition assertion passes for the wrong reason in the real ordering (the job errors with 节点不存在 rather than being executed), and its ② assertion passes only because of the pre-population it performs itself. So the gate is a necessary but insufficient condition here, exactly as the task warned, and the remaining false-green is assertion-side rather than implementation-side. Separately, and reported as a finding, the mutation self-check now reports 21/27 against this working tree; those six failures are expected consequences of the fix coexisting with the baseline assertions, and they mean the teeth-evidence is no longer reproducible here without the pre-fix revision.

I attacked each explicitly-uncovered gap with my own out-of-repo probes (TEMPORARY directory, repo node_modules via junction and repo React so the real hook could run; no repository file added or modified). Constraint (a) paused loophole: EXCLUDED — the guard does not read paused at all (:226-244); with paused=true a triple click still admitted exactly 1 and a batch of 4 was still admitted whole (4/4), matching the comment at :77-78 and confirming the paused-state loophole class is closed. Constraint (b) synchronous inside enqueue: EXCLUDED — the decision is synchronous in enqueue with no await, and since retry calls enqueue in-process it is covered; the gate's case E (non-awaited overlapping clicks) and case F (retry) also pass. Constraint (e) never running-only and (d) active-only: EXCLUDED — isActiveJob is queued||running (:101-103) and historical success/error/cancelled jobs neither block a new click nor block retry (probe: after forcing all jobs terminal, a fresh batch of 4 was admitted; retry added exactly 1). Constraint (f) node-scoped, not global: EXCLUDED — two different nodeIds each admitted their own batch while both were active. Constraint (c) batch atomicity: HOLDS for the real caller — a 4-job click is admitted whole and a second complete click is rejected in full (0 growth), because the continuation chain matches on shape key plus the exact next index; I could not truncate a legitimate batch through the hook, and the alternative failure (a legitimate batch blocked by a stale chain) also did not occur because each new click's first call overwrites or deletes the chain. enqueue returning "" instead of an id: THIS IS A LIVE PROBLEM — the only production callers are useImageGeneratorExecution.ts:63 and :76, and neither inspects the return value, while the hook writes {queued:true,status:"idle"} unconditionally at :86-90; the result is reported as Finding 2 (a rejected click permanently locks the node, reproduced 3/3 with the button-enablement window captured). The retry caller (queueStore.retry) also ignores the return value, but its failure mode is benign (a no-op) and is what the gate's case F sanity-checks. Batch-chain integrity across nodes/canvases/cancel/retry/rehydration: same-node-same-shape interference, cross-node interference, mid-batch cancel (the same click's remaining calls were still admitted), retry interleaved with a batch click, and retry followed by a fresh batch (no enqueueOriginRetry leak, since retry resets it in finally at :289-292) all behaved correctly; the residual hazards are the cross-canvas nodeId collision (Finding 3, live) and the interrupted-loop desync (Finding 4, latent/not currently reachable). REQ-001's cold-start path is the other live failure (Finding 1).

The design is defensible in its main line: keeping the decision inside enqueue (rather than a module-level boolean or a global lock) is what makes it cover retry and non-awaited clicks, and the shape-key plus next-index model avoids timers, so it is not timing-dependent for the single-canvas case. Two concrete reservations, both code-evidenced. First, correctness rests on an invariant that lives only in prose: a click's batch loop must start at batchIndex 1 and run to completion without an await (:61-74, guarded by comments at queueStore.ts:63-73). Nothing enforces it, and a probe that interrupted a batch after its first of four jobs showed a subsequent identical-shape click being misread as a continuation, admitting 3 extra jobs. Today that trigger is not reachable (the loop is synchronous and cannot throw, since executeImageGeneration is async), so I rank it latent rather than live — but it is exactly the kind of hidden coupling that turns into a false-green later, and a hook-side batch token (or a remaining-count in the chain instead of index arithmetic) would remove the dependency entirely. Second, the module-level state is unbounded and not lifecycle-aware: batchChains is only ever deleted for the same nodeId on a later single/retry enqueue (:241-243) and is never cleared on rehydration or canvas switch, even though the queue itself bounds jobs at 200 (:249); and enqueueOriginRetry is a module-global that is only safe because enqueue is synchronous and retry resets it in a finally — a future await inside enqueue, or a second caller of retry, would silently break the provenance distinction. Both are cheap to harden (clear the map in onRehydrateStorage, pass the origin flag as an explicit parameter or an argument-level wrapper instead of module state). I do not recommend a structural split of the module on line-count grounds; at 449 lines it is cohesive, and the recovery/waiting helpers are already top-level functions rather than store methods. The one genuine cohesion cost is that the module now owns three concerns that interact subtly — persistence/recovery, the duplicate-admission guard, and scheduling (pump) — which is what lets an enqueue-side rejection contract silently disagree with a hook-side caller; documenting that contract at the call site (useImageGeneratorExecution.ts:61-90) would address the real risk.

The change is performance-neutral on the hot path. The guard adds one linear scan of the in-memory jobs array for the node's active jobs (hasActiveJobForNode, :106-108) plus, for batched clicks only, a small string key build (:111-120, joining at most six fields with one JSON.stringify of dataOverride, which is a constant {n:1} in the real caller); jobs are capped at 200 by the slice in enqueue (:249), so per-click cost is bounded and negligible relative to a network image-generation call, and no timers, polling or extra I/O are introduced. The recovery path adds one bounded wait loop (:172-181, 25ms interval, 600ms deadline) that runs at most once per process (recoveryStarted, :149), so its cost is bounded and it cannot spin or delay startup beyond 600ms in the worst case; waitForCanvasReady's resumable dynamic imports are cached after first use. The only footprint observation, already reported under maintainability, is that batchChains is a module-level Map that is never pruned and grows by one small entry per distinct nodeId that begins a batch; that is a slow, bounded-in-practice memory consideration, not a hot-path cost, and it does not change this verdict. No throughput, latency or rendering regression is plausible from this diff.
